solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Spooner’s one not revealing partner that’s web-user under cover (5,6)

indicatorNotes.Spooner’s: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version of a phrase is the answer

blocks.note: a partner is a spouse; it gives up its SP sound for the H of the next word
one who does not reveal something is a hider; it takes the SP in exchange for its H

annotation.surface: A secretive person keeping their other half out of sight, and something lurking unseen.
annotation.walkthrough: The Spooner swap works on sounds: SP-OUSE H-IDER becomes H-OUSE SP-IDER. 'Under cover' means indoors, where a house spider spins its web.
annotation.definitionFit: A house spider is the web-spinning spider that lives indoors, under a roof.

entries.clue: Bean counter’s head lowered in carriage (7)

indicatorNotes.head: the head of a word is its first letter
indicatorNotes.lowered: in a down clue, lowering a letter moves it further down the column, later in the word

blocks.note: a chariot is a horse-drawn carriage
first letter of counter; the C at the top of CHARIOT drops to near the bottom

annotation.surface: An accountant sitting in a carriage with head bowed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bean counter' is a ready-made phrase for an accountant, but the definition is just 'Bean'. Drop the C of CHARIOT two places down the column.
annotation.definitionFit: The haricot is a common bean, the one used for baked beans.

entries.clue: Handy huts serf built at regular intervals (6)

indicatorNotes.at regular intervals: take letters at a fixed spacing, here every second one

blocks.note: hUtS sErF bUiLt: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on

annotation.surface: A medieval peasant putting up some convenient sheds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Built' looks like an anagram indicator, but it is part of the letter string being sampled.
annotation.definitionFit: Handy and useful both describe something that serves a purpose.

entries.clue: Very game opponents displaying elevated coldness in friendly (10)

indicatorNotes.elevated: in a down clue, raising a word writes it bottom to top
indicatorNotes.in: the reversed ice goes inside the word for friendly

blocks.note: in bridge, East and South are opponents
pally = friendly, P…ALLY holding the next block
ice = coldness, raised to ECI

annotation.surface: Two keen sporting rivals showing a bit of frostiness in a friendly match.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Very game' reads as 'very keen', but the definition stops at 'Very'; 'friendly' looks like a noun (a friendly match) and is really the adjective PALLY. ES + P(ECI)ALLY.
annotation.definitionFit: Very and especially are both intensifiers: very good, especially good.

entries.clue: Bird taking off in gust (4)

indicatorNotes.taking off: removing: the word IN is taken off the bird

blocks.note: the puffin is a seabird
the word itself, read literally as the two letters to take off the bird's tail

annotation.surface: A bird taking flight in a strong wind.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Taking off' and 'gust' paint a bird in flight; here 'taking off' means removing, and 'in' is the literal word to remove.
annotation.definitionFit: A puff is a short gust of wind or breath.

entries.clue: Diary regularly seen with delicate visual aid (8)

indicatorNotes.regularly: at regular intervals, so the letters are sampled at an even spacing: here every other one

blocks.note: DiArY: first, third and fifth letters
light = delicate, as in a light touch

annotation.surface: A diary kept alongside some fine instrument for seeing.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Visual aid' suggests a chart or a pair of glasses; daylight is an aid to seeing in the most literal sense.
annotation.definitionFit: Daylight helps you see, so it is quite literally a visual aid.

entries.clue: Get on case after second bit of evidence goes missing (7)

indicatorNotes.after: the case follows ON in the answer
indicatorNotes.goes missing: something that goes missing is no longer there, so the V vanishes from the case

blocks.note: re = on, concerning
a valise is a small travelling case; drop its V
second letter of eVidence, the one that goes missing

annotation.surface: A detective getting on the case once a piece of evidence disappears.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a police procedural, with 'Get on case' as one phrase. The definition is just 'Get', as in 'I get it'. RE + (V)ALISE.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the informal sense of 'get' as grasp or understand, as in 'I get the joke'.

entries.clue: Divide fish keeping endlessly even and uniform (5,2)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the fish holds the other letters inside it
indicatorNotes.endlessly: both ends are removed from even

blocks.note: the carp is a freshwater fish, CAR…P around the rest
EVEN without its first and last letters
U is Uniform in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Splitting up a fish into equal, identical portions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Even and uniform' reads as a pair of adjectives about the portions; they are two separate pieces. CAR(VE + U)P.
annotation.definitionFit: A phrasal verb from slicing a joint of meat, used figuratively for sharing out land, spoils or a market.

entries.clue: After couple of drinks, play equipment to make dance song (3-3,5)

blocks.note: cha is slang for tea, so two teas are CHA CHA
a slide in a playground

annotation.surface: A couple of drinks, a go on the playground slide, and a party song.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Play equipment' suggests a sports kit or instruments; it is the playground kind. 'Cha' is British slang for tea.
annotation.definitionFit: The Cha-Cha Slide is a 2000 party song that calls out its own dance steps.

entries.clue: Zoom with AI character and fine team player (3,4)

blocks.note: to fly = to zoom along
HAL 9000 is the computer in 2001: A Space Odyssey
F = fine, on pencil leads

annotation.surface: A video call with an AI chatbot and a talented teammate.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Zoom' and 'AI' point at modern tech; the chunks are FLY, HAL and F. A fly-half is a rugby position, the playmaker who wears number 10.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the rugby position is one member of a fifteen-player team.

entries.clue: Deftly with hand, I performed card trick (4,3,4)

indicatorNotes.performed: the letters are worked into a new arrangement

blocks.note: anagram fodder
anagram fodder

annotation.surface: A magician boasting of a sleight-of-hand trick done nimbly.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue sounds like a conjuror; 'deftly' and 'hand' are simply letters. Find the lady is the three-card trick where you must spot the queen.
annotation.definitionFit: Find the lady is a card trick, often a street hustle, in which the punter tracks the queen.

entries.clue: A group receiving tips for cardiovascular exercise (2,6)

indicatorNotes.receiving: the group takes other letters into it
indicatorNotes.tips: a word's tips are its two pointed ends, so its first and last letters

blocks.note: A as printed
a bunch is a group, B…UNCH around the tips
the first and last letters of cardiovascular

annotation.surface: A gym class getting advice on cardio.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cardiovascular exercise' sits together as the phrase for running or cycling; the definition is only 'exercise', and 'for' belongs to the tips. An ab crunch works the abdominal muscles, not the heart.
annotation.definitionFit: An ab crunch is a sit-up style exercise for the abdominal muscles.

entries.clue: Object returned, carried by stray hairy beast (6)

indicatorNotes.returned: the word is sent back, written right to left
indicatorNotes.carried by: the reversed word is held inside the next one

blocks.note: to sin is to stray from virtue, S…IN around the rest
an aim is an object or goal, returned to MIA

annotation.surface: A lost item handed back by a shaggy stray animal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Object' looks like a verb, and 'stray' like a stray dog; object is AIM, and stray is the verb SIN. SI(MIA)N.
annotation.definitionFit: Simian means an ape or monkey, a hairy beast.

entries.clue: Somehow see such turmoil might be serendipitous (10)

indicatorNotes.Somehow: the letters are combined in some unspecified order
indicatorNotes.might be: the combined letters could be rearranged to spell serendipitous

blocks.note: the thirteen letters the whole mixes to
take these letters out of serendipitous; what remains is the fodder
points at the definition: see plus such turmoil, the unknown word, mix to serendipitous

annotation.surface: An optimist insisting that chaos could turn out to be a happy accident.
annotation.walkthrough: This is a composite anagram: SEE plus the answer rearranges to SERENDIPITOUS. So the answer is the letters of serendipitous left once S, E, E are struck out.
annotation.definitionFit: Disruption and turmoil both mean disorder and upheaval.

entries.clue: Detest fifth choice of headwear? (4)

blocks.note: a hat is headwear
in a list of options A, B, C, D, E, the fifth is E

annotation.surface: Grumbling at being offered a fifth-rate hat.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the trick: 'fifth choice of headwear' is HAT option E, as on a multiple-choice form.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both verbs mean to loathe intensely.

entries.clue: Party protecting popular revolutionary fellows ultimately against exile (10)

indicatorNotes.protecting: the party wraps around the next piece
indicatorNotes.ultimately: ultimately means in the end, so the word's end: its last letter

blocks.note: a bash is a party, BA…SH around the next piece
in = popular, turned round to NI
fellows = men
last letter of against

annotation.surface: A political party sheltering a well-liked radical and his comrades, in the end opposed to deportation.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Popular revolutionary' reads as a folk hero, but 'revolutionary' just reverses IN. BA(NI)SH + MEN + T.
annotation.definitionFit: Exile and banishment are both forced removal from one's country.

entries.clue: Comparatively wet week at lake with onset of rain (8)

indicatorNotes.onset of: the start, so the first letter

blocks.note: W = week
as printed
Lake Erie, one of the Great Lakes
first letter of rain

annotation.surface: A rainier week than usual at a lakeside holiday.
annotation.walkthrough: Every word fits the holiday picture; 'with' just joins the last piece on.
annotation.definitionFit: Waterier is the comparative of watery, so more wet.

entries.clue: Sales girl merrily welcomes new comms people (10)

indicatorNotes.merrily: the letters dance about into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder
N = new, taken in

annotation.surface: A cheerful shop assistant greeting some new staff from the communications team.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sales girl' reads as one person; its nine letters plus N mix to the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: Signallers send messages, as in the army's signals corps, so they are communications people.

entries.clue: City’s luminosity inspiring when on top of Gherkin (7)

indicatorNotes.inspiring: breathing in, so holding the next pieces inside
indicatorNotes.on top of: in a down clue, placed above
indicatorNotes.Gherkin: only its first letter is used, as its top

blocks.note: glow = luminosity, GL…OW around the rest
as = when, as in 'as I left'
first letter of Gherkin, with AS on top of it

annotation.surface: A city skyline lit up, with the Gherkin tower at its peak.
annotation.walkthrough: The Gherkin is a London skyscraper, so the surface points to London; the city is Glasgow. GL(AS + G)OW.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the answer is one example of a city, Scotland's largest.

entries.clue: Told what’s predetermined for holiday (4)

indicatorNotes.Told: said, so the answer sounds like a word

blocks.note: fate is what is predetermined; fête is pronounced the same

annotation.surface: Someone being told their holiday plans were settled in advance.
annotation.walkthrough: Fête is said like fate. The definition is fair because a fête is a festival day.
annotation.definitionFit: A fête is a festival or holiday, a day of celebration.

entries.clue: Female ruler gets cross replacing third in command, say (7)

indicatorNotes.replacing: taking the place of, so one letter swaps out and another goes in

blocks.note: an empress is a female ruler
X is a cross, and goes in
the third letter of command, which comes out of the ruler

annotation.surface: A queen losing her temper and taking over as the number three in command.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Third in command' reads as a rank; it is the third letter of the word command. 'Gets cross' is not anger but the letter X taking the M's place.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to express a view is to say it, put it into words.

entries.clue: American ready, tackling disheartened pal’s depression (6)

indicatorNotes.tackling: taking on, so wrapping around the next piece
indicatorNotes.disheartened: the heart, or middle letter, is removed

blocks.note: ready is slang for cash; a dime is a US ten-cent coin, DIM…E around the rest
PAL without its middle letter

annotation.surface: An American ready to help a friend through a low mood.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Depression' and 'disheartened' conspire to suggest low spirits; the answer is a small hollow. 'Ready' as a noun is money, as in 'the readies'.
annotation.definitionFit: A dimple is a small depression in the skin or a surface.

entries.clue: Enchanting person captured in extremely injurious pictures (6)

indicatorNotes.extremely: the extremes, the first and last letters

blocks.note: the first and last letters of injurious, I…S around the rest
a mage is a magician, someone who casts spells

annotation.surface: A sorcerer caught on camera in some damaging photographs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Enchanting person' suggests someone charming; it is a spell-caster. I(MAGE)S.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: photographs and drawings are both pictures and images.

entries.clue: Peach fruit cut as ingredient for stew, perhaps (5,3)

indicatorNotes.cut: the fruit loses its last letter

blocks.note: to peach and to split are both slang for informing on someone
PEAR without its last letter

annotation.surface: A peach sliced up to go in a stew.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Peach fruit' looks like one thing; 'Peach' is the old verb meaning to inform, as is split. The stew is the pea soup kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Split peas are dried peas that go into soups and stews.

entries.clue: Appear quiet with nothing being brought up (4)

indicatorNotes.being brought up: in a down clue, raised so it reads bottom to top

blocks.note: sh! means be quiet
W = with
O looks like zero; W then O is raised to OW

annotation.surface: Staying silent and not raising anything, to be seen.
annotation.walkthrough: SH stays put; only W + O is raised to OW.
annotation.definitionFit: To show is to appear, as in 'he didn't show'.

entries.clue: Like Chas & Dave, maybe remix hit single after releasing it (7)

indicatorNotes.remix: mix the letters again into a new order
indicatorNotes.releasing: letting go of IT, so removing it

blocks.note: the letters to mix
removed from hit single, leaving H SINGLE

annotation.surface: A remix of a Chas & Dave hit record.
annotation.walkthrough: Chas & Dave were a London duo known for cockney pub singalongs, so English describes them. 'Maybe' marks them as one example.
annotation.definitionFit: Chas & Dave were English musicians, so they are an example of English people.

entries.clue: Mischief-maker that is totally discharged for irreverence (7)

indicatorNotes.discharged: emptied of its contents, leaving only the outer letters

blocks.note: an imp is a mischievous child or sprite
i.e. = id est, that is
TOTALLY emptied, leaving T…Y

annotation.surface: A troublemaker fired outright for being cheeky.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Totally discharged' reads as sacked outright; 'discharged' means emptied of its middle letters.
annotation.definitionFit: Impiety is a lack of reverence, especially for God.

entries.clue: Employees gathering got leader to definitively make improvements (4,7)

blocks.note: workers = employees, WORK…ERS around the rest
won = got, gained
first letter of definitively

annotation.surface: Staff rallying behind a boss who makes things better once and for all.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Leader' suggests a boss; it gives only the first letter of 'definitively'. WORK(WON + D)ERS.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom: working wonders means achieving remarkable results, usually making something much better.
